questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes why a propositional sentence must be in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) before applying the resolution rule?

options.A: Resolution can only combine literals that appear in the same clause, which is guaranteed by CNF.
options.B: CNF ensures that every clause is a Horn clause, making resolution complete.
options.C: In CNF each clause is a disjunction of literals, allowing the resolution rule to eliminate a complementary pair of literals.
options.D: CNF converts all implications into biconditionals, which are required for resolution.

questions.explanation:
The resolution rule is defined for sentences that are a conjunction of clauses, where each clause is a disjunction of literals; this form enables the elimination of complementary literals (Page 180).  

---

questions.question: Given a knowledge base consisting only of Horn clauses, which inference rule is guaranteed to be complete for deriving any entailed atomic sentence?

options.D: Forward chaining using the Horn‑clause rule

questions.explanation:
Horn clauses are of the form (α₁∧…∧αₙ)⇒β, and forward‑chaining (the Horn‑clause rule) is complete for Horn KBs (Page 180).

questions.question: If the TT‑CHECK‑ALL algorithm is invoked on a propositional KB with n distinct symbols, what is the worst‑case time complexity of the algorithm?
questions.explanation:
The algorithm explores all possible truth assignments; the text states the cost is O(2ⁿ) for n symbols (Page 184).

questions.question: According to the definition of logical entailment in the notes, the statement “KB ⊨ α” is true exactly when which of the following conditions holds?

options.A: The conjunction (KB ∧ α) is a tautology.
options.D: The implication (KB ⇒ α) is false in at least one model.

questions.explanation: The text defines entailment as KB ⊨ α iff (KB ∧ ¬α) is unsatisfiable (Page 180).
